name: Federal criminal cases by offense and district (U.S. Courts Tables D-1, D-2 and D-3)
description: Criminal defendants whose cases were opened in the 94 federal district courts, counted from the Statistical Tables for the Federal Judiciary that the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts publishes for each 12-month period ending June 30 and December 31. Each record gives one district, one state with more than one district, or the whole country, for one period: the defendants commenced (transfers between districts left out), split by offense into nineteen columns and ten offense groups, with drug, immigration (illegal reentry shown on its own), firearms, fraud, sex offenses and traffic picked out, the felony, Class A misdemeanor and petty-offense split from Table D-1, and the same period a year earlier. National records add Table D-2's detail of about a hundred offenses, from bank robbery and health-care fraud to drunk driving on federal land. Every period's districts add up to the national total printed by the Courts, and every district ties to Table D-1.
citeAs: Probative Growth. (2026). Federal criminal cases by offense and district (U.S. Courts Tables D-1, D-2 and D-3) (Version 2.0.0) [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23963315

distribution.name: criminal-filings.csv
distribution.description: Every record, one row each (RFC 4180, UTF-8). Columns are described in README.txt.

distribution.name: criminal-filings.json
distribution.description: Every record with its full sources, under a meta envelope (credit line, DOI, license).

distribution.name: criminal-filings-values.csv
distribution.description: The columns listed in README.txt as being in criminal-filings-values.csv, one row per id, column and value; join it to criminal-filings.csv on id.

field.name: id
field.description: Stable record id (never reused)

field.name: jurisdiction
field.description: Two-letter code of the state or territory the district sits in, or US

field.name: level
field.description: district (one federal judicial district), state (the sum of a state's districts; only states with more than one) or us (all 94 districts)

field.name: periodStart
field.description: First day of the 12-month period

field.name: periodEnd
field.description: Last day of the 12-month period (June 30 or December 31)

field.name: latest
field.description: true for the newest period the Courts have published

field.name: status
field.description: P primary source, S secondary source

field.name: text

field.name: value

field.name: unit

field.name: defendants
field.description: Criminal defendants whose cases were opened in the district in the period, excluding defendants transferred in from another district (Table D-3 Total). One person charged in two cases counts twice.
